Subject: Post-demo: Redwood Inference - Buying committee recap & next steps

Hi Alex (and team),

Thanks again for your time today — appreciate everyone on the buying committee joining the demo. Quick recap of what we covered, the stakeholders we identified, decision criteria, and proposed next steps so we’re all aligned.

What we demoed
- Hosted API and Dedicated options: how traffic routing and fallbacks work
- Private (VPC) deployment: KMS integration and audit log examples
- Cost/perf tradeoffs: batching, KV cache, quantization profiles
- Console: per-route dashboards + rollout controls

Attendees / stakeholder mapping (as we captured):
- Alex Johnson — Head of AI (primary champion) / technical evaluation
- Evan Clarke — CTO / economic buyer (high-level budget approval)
- Judy Park — Head of Security (security questionnaire + controls)
- Samir Patel — Procurement Manager (contract & PO)
- Procurement Legal — TBD (contract redlines)

Primary decision criteria we heard
- Performance: p95 latency <= 200ms for 512-token prompts under expected load
- Security & compliance: SOC 2 Type II, KMS support, audit logs, data deletion controls
- Deployment flexibility: option for VPC/private + on-prem evaluation if required by legal
- Unit economics: committed monthly capacity with predictable pricing and overage rules

Immediate next steps (proposed timeline)
1) We will share SOC 2 report, security answers, and pricing sheet (today) — action: Marissa
2) Schedule a technical security workshop between Redwood Security & Nexa Security (by next Wed) — action: Judy / Dylan to coordinate
3) Procurement to share contract process & sample timelines (Alex/Samir) — action: Samir
4) Draft SOW/PO target: goal is to have PO or signed SOW by end of Q2 (moving faster if possible)

Attachments: pricing-sheet.xlsx (pricing bands), demo-recording.mp4 (recording).

Would you confirm the stakeholder list above and if the timeline looks reasonable? If so I’ll get the docs over and propose 2-3 times for the security workshop.

Thanks,

Marissa — thanks for the clear recap. Confirming the stakeholder list looks right from our side. A few clarifications / asks from procurement & legal before we lock timeline:

- Legal will need ~2 weeks to review any contract with standard redlines; if you can share a draft SOW and sample MSA (or markups) that will help speed that up.
- Procurement (Samir) — we usually do an initial pricing review and then request 3rd-party references for SLA-backed deployments (happy to provide reference customers for Dedicated).

- Pricing: please include a line for Dedicated capacity blocks + overage rates and any discounts for annual commitment.

Samir — looping you in for procurement timeline (Samir, can you confirm the typical time from contract start to PO on your side?).

Happy to meet for the technical workshop; Tue/Thu next week mornings PT work for me.

Thanks Alex — quick technical notes to add ahead of the security workshop:

- KMS: we support customer-managed keys via AWS KMS / GCP KMS / Azure Key Vault for both Private and Dedicated deployments. Keys are never persisted outside the customer KMS.
- Data residency: Private deployments run inside customer VPCs; for Hosted we can restrict regions and we keep separate logs per account.
- Deletion/retention: we have configurable retention windows; we can set up automatic KV cache TTLs and deletion hooks tied to your data lifecycle policies.
- SOC 2: attaching our SOC 2 Type II redacted report and a one-page security answers PDF for Judy.

Attached: security-answers.pdf

I can join the security workshop to walk through architecture and encryption flows. Proposed slots: Wed 10–11am PT or Thu 9–10am PT.

Thanks,
Dylan Brooks
